items.text:
Divide and conquer - now maverick Erasmus plans online watchalong
- Published
Having been banned from the touchline for six matches, you will not find Rassie Erasmus at the Aviva Stadium when his South Africa side face Ireland.
Instead he will be hosting an online watchalong of Saturday's match, courtesy of a swiftly purchased domain name.
The South Africa head coach plans to stream his reactions live while watching on television from his team's Dublin hotel.
It is typical Erasmus. An unapologetic, unabashed show of defiance in the face of the authorities.
And he will not be short of virtual company.
Because, while Erasmus has run low of advocates elsewhere, his compatriots have rushed to his defence.
"Rassie was just asking questions," said former South Africa hooker Hanyani Shimange in the wake of Erasmus' ban for a scattergun series of complaints about the injustices suffered by his side.
"But you have to look at the facts. Where was the accountability for that refereeing performance [in the loss to France]?"
Naas Botha, legendary South Africa fly-half turned pundit, described Erasmus' punishment as a "debacle". "You can't tell me [officials] are untouchable," he said.
Supersport, which broadcasts South Africa's games domestically, published an article accusing Erasmus' critics of "pearl clutching", external and "shooting the messenger" with regards to the game's faults.
Despite slurring officials with a suggestion of match-fixing, Erasmus has the support of South Africa.
It is not surprising.
His feats with the team are astonishing.
South Africa were ranked sixth in the world when he took over in March 2018.
He arrived after a November tour in which they lost to Wales and were thrashed 38-3 by Ireland. New Zealand had racked up a record 57-0 win a few months earlier.
Erasmus turned the team around at speed, marrying their trademark up-front power with pace out wide.
They won the 2019 World Cup. The defended their title in 2023. They will go into the tournament in 2027 aiming for an unprecedented hat-trick. And few would bet against them achieving it.
Erasmus is relentlessly innovative.
Long before the sport's data revolution, he was coding game footage, picking up the technique from a friend who worked in the military. He has since developed Outfox, his own software which allows his teams to run through moves virtually on a screen away from the pitch.
Tactically, he has also been ahead of the curve. He pioneered the use of forward-heavy replacement benches, giving his team an edge in the final quarter of the match.
He saw the game-breaking potential of diminutive Sevens specialist Kurt-Lee Arendse and moulded Andre Esterhuizen into a genuine hybrid player, capable of playing in the back row and the backline.
Trick plays - forcing a scrum with a deliberate infringement off kick-off, or setting up a line-out in the middle of the pitch - have been part of Erasmus' arsenal.
Legally, he is across every possible loophole.
There was controversy before the match against France last weekend when he made use of the Nations Championships' looser regulations to swap his starting front row just over an hour before kick-off.
Previously, he demoted himself to water boy so he could run the touchline during the 2021 series win over the British and Irish Lions.
Former Springbok wing Bryan Habana worked under Erasmus at the Stormers in Cape Town.
"He is one of the master tacticians the game has ever seen," Habana told BBC Sport's Ireland Rugby Social.
"I don't always agree with how Rassie comes across, but I understand he wears his heart on his sleeve. He has got incredibly high standards.
"He's willing to be in the firing line to defend what he believes is right."
But there is no doubt, by the letter of the law, that Erasmus is wrong - certainly in terms of the platform and terms he chose for his complaints.
In July World Rugby introduced new rules around criticism of officials. It specifically targeted "comments which, viewed objectively, a reasonable person would conclude were an attack on the credibility or competence of the match officials".
Mentioning "match-fixing" undermines the officials in exactly that way.
Considering Erasmus' previous, including an hour-long monologue bemoaning officiating of a first-Test defeat by the Lions in 2021 and a series of tweets after a loss to France a year later, he may be fortunate to only be banned for six matches.
World Rugby, perhaps pre-empting the reaction in South Africa, was clear that it was not punishing Erasmus for asking questions.
"Robust, respectful debate is natural, but teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches," it said in its judgement.
"Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse."
For many South Africans, though, Erasmus is still an outlaw hero.
World Rugby, based in Dublin, is seen by them as tilted towards the north.
Australian Brett Robinson, the current chairman, is the first figure from outside the Six Nations countries to hold the organisation's top job since it became an elected position.
The World Cup has been lifted by South Africa on four occasions, but held there only once.
Japan coach Eddie Jones, Erasmus' fellow maverick, recently suggested Ireland's political clout, external was behind his team's home game being staged in Australia rather than Tokyo.
South Africa were a powerful voice against the possible moves to "depower" the scrum - a key part of the Springbok game - at a February conference to discuss future law tweaks.
Erasmus' public pronouncements have fuelled conspiracy theories weaved from those threads. They have also made an all-time great team harder for outsiders to love.
Whether it is a deliberate ploy is hard to tell.
Certainly Erasmus is a repeat offender, but his offences have also come in his second language. He is an Afrikaans speaker.

items.summary:
Alex Scott: Arsenal keen on Chelsea and Liverpool target with Bournemouth softening stance over potential sale
Premier League champions Arsenal would require a sale to accommodate Alex Scott in their midfield and it is understood they would be willing to make a change in that department to beat riva
items.text:
Alex Scott: Arsenal keen on Chelsea and Liverpool target with Bournemouth softening stance over potential sale
Premier League champions Arsenal would require a sale to accommodate Alex Scott in their midfield and it is understood they would be willing to make a change in that department to beat rivals Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature with Bournemouth demanding up to £100m
Tuesday 17 November 2026 20:34, UK
Arsenal are one of three top Premier League clubs interested in signing Bournemouth and England midfielder Alex Scott.
Sky Sports News understands the Premier League champions would be willing to make changes in midfield to beat Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature.
Discussions about Arsenal's 2027 transfer plans are believed to have taken place between manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta already.
It is understood they would need to sell at least one of their current midfielders to facilitate a deal for Scott in January or next summer.

With Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly all doing so well this season, Mikel Merino is arguably the most likely candidate having struggled for game time. He has made only one Premier League start and said last week while on Spain duty that he wants more minutes.
His club and country team-mate Martin Zubimendi could be another candidate, although illness and injury have impacted his minutes so far this campaign and he has impressed recently when he has played. There is still a long way to go in the season and any injury to a key midfielder could impact Arsenal's ideas.
Merino said while on Spain duty: "We know what our roles are, and we're both calm and eager to keep training hard to show that we can continue to be there." But he also said: "Not being on the pitch most of the time isn't ideal for a player. Arsenal is currently the best team in the world, and it's very difficult to get minutes."
Scott is likely to be one of the biggest names potentially on the January transfer market, with Bournemouth believed to have softened their stance on the idea of a sale, having been unable to agree a new contract with the 23-year-old.
However, they will still command a high fee for the England international, hoping for close to £100m including add-ons. Sources have indicated something around £75m to £80m plus bonuses could get a deal done.
Bournemouth are also going strongly this season however, including in the Europa League. Should that continue, they may feel keeping Scott until next summer would give them a better chance of going far in the competition and securing European football again for next season.
Chelsea also remain persistent with their interest in Scott, and they are believed to have the financial edge on other clubs - but he is not their only target.
Manager Xabi Alonso remains open to signing another midfielder after the departure of Enzo Fernandez in the summer, although Romeo Lavia's improvement has lessened the necessity, after seeing a deadline-day deal for Lamine Camara of Monaco fall down in the summer.
Liverpool are keen to add to their midfield options in the longer term, and they see Scott as the perfect option to add some guile and passing ability to their squad.
Scott was a key part of Andoni Iraola's system at Bournemouth before the Spanish coach moved to Anfield. He remains a big admirer and there is a wider belief at Liverpool that he could also be a key tactical piece in Iraola's plans going forward.
Scott will have only 12 months left on his existing deal next summer, at which point his value will reduce.
Arsenal tracking Nusa and Schade in winger search
Latest from Sky Sports News' Adrian Kajumba and Lyall Thomas:
Arsenal are continuing to track the likes of RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and Brentford's Kevin Schade as they assess potential forward options ahead of improving their squad in 2027.
Adding a marquee name to their attack was one of the objectives Arsenal were unable to tick-off during the summer window, failing to agree deals for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Jr, Bradley Barcola and Julian Alvarez.
With Alvarez not keen to leave Spain, the Gunners are believed to be moving on from their pursuit of the Argentina star and assessing again how to improve in attack, primarily on the left side but with someone versatile enough to operate across the frontline.
A move for Nusa is now something Arsenal are keen to progress with, sources have told Sky Sports News, but he is not the only potential target they are monitoring.
Sky Sports News revealed their admiration for Schade last month amid the forward's talks with Brentford over a new contract.
Nusa, who has two-and-a-half years left on his Leipzig deal, has no exit clause so a deal would need to be negotiated - and Leipzig do not want to sell him January come-what-may, according to other sources, so a move next summer seems more feasible as things stand.
Nusa actually almost signed for Brentford in the summer they brought in Schade from Freiburg.
Nicknamed the Norwegian Neymar after his childhood hero, Nusa is an international team-mate of Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard and has been on the radar of Premier League clubs for some time.
He is now into his third season and producing his best performances to date. The 21-year-old has directly contributed to 14 goals in just 15 games in all competitions this season, with six goals and eight assists.
One of his goals was a Champions League strike against Manchester City earlier this month and this season's efforts add to the 10 goals and 11 assists he recorded across his first two seasons at the German club.

items.title: Ruto takes veiled swipe at Gachagua over Mt Kenya voting bloc politics
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto has taken a veiled swipe at former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua over his political mobilisation in the Mt Kenya region, declaring that no community should be reduced to a voting bloc.
In his State of the Nation Address to Parliament on Wednesday,
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto has taken a veiled swipe at former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua over his political mobilisation in the Mt Kenya region, declaring that no community should be reduced to a voting bloc.
In his State of the Nation Address to Parliament on Wednesday, Ruto challenged political leaders against asking entire regions to surrender their political choices to individual personalities, insisting that voters should assess leaders on their proposals and performance.
“No community should be reduced to a voting bloc. No region should be asked to surrender its judgement to a personality,” he said.
Although he did not mention Gachagua by name, the remarks came amid the former Deputy President’s efforts to consolidate the Mt Kenya region behind his Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), which he has increasingly presented as an alternative political home for the region.
Gachagua has repeatedly described Mt Kenya as a DCP stronghold and urged residents to reject the ruling party and incumbent lawmakers allied to it, whom he has branded “traitors”.
His mobilisation received a boost on Tuesday when he welcomed three sitting lawmakers who had abandoned Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA) for DCP.
The DCP leader received Gatundu South MP Gabriel Kagombe, whose defection party hardliners had put on hold since August, alongside Nyeri Woman Representative Rahab Mukami and Laikipia West MP Wachira Karani.
Receiving the legislators at his Wamunyoro residence, Gachagua described DCP as “the party of the moment and the future”, declaring that the “transfer window” for UDA members would remain open until December 31, 2026.
“All politics is local. A defining moment for Mlima politics,” he said.
He also noted that DCP had grown from nineteen to twenty-five members following the latest political movements and expressed confidence that the party would have sixty MPs by next year.
The former Deputy President has been seeking to consolidate support in the region following his fallout with Ruto and his impeachment in October 2024.
Other prominent politicians who have joined DCP include Murang’a Governor Irungu Kang’ata, Nakuru Senator Tabitha Karanja and Nyandarua Governor Kiarie Badilisha.
Ruto, in his SONA speech appared to push back on Gachagua’s rhetoric, saying citizens should be able to assess those seeking public office based on what they propose, how they intend to deliver and how their performance will be measured.
“That standard applies first to those of us entrusted with Government. We must account for our commitments and our record. Those who offer alternatives must explain their proposals. All of us must respect the people’s right to question, scrutinise and choose,” he said.
The President called for serious political debate on production, employment, education, healthcare, infrastructure and national opportunity, urging leaders to move beyond personality-driven politics.
He challenged political actors to explain how they would lower electricity costs, finance infrastructure, expand employment, improve healthcare and make education more accessible.
Ruto said proposals should be assessed against evidence, commitments against available resources and promises against results.
The President also cited the national conversation launched in August 2026 on Kenya’s development beyond 2030, calling for a development charter reflecting shared aspirations and commitments capable of enduring beyond electoral cycles.

items.title: Sifuna dismisses Ruto’s fourth State of the Nation Address as ‘State of Imagination’
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 – Linda Mwananchi Party leader Edwin Sifuna has criticised President William Ruto’s fourth State of the Nation Address, accusing him of failing to address the constitutional requirements of the annual presidential report and instead focusing on development projects.
Sifuna arg
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 – Linda Mwananchi Party leader Edwin Sifuna has criticised President William Ruto’s fourth State of the Nation Address, accusing him of failing to address the constitutional requirements of the annual presidential report and instead focusing on development projects.
Sifuna argued that Article 132 of the Constitution requires the President to report to Parliament on the steps taken and progress achieved in realising the national values and principles of governance outlined under Article 10.
He maintained that the address should focus on issues such as respect for human rights, the rule of law, democracy, equality, freedom of citizens and public participation rather than a catalogue of roads, markets and other infrastructure projects.
“The Constitution of Kenya, in Article 132, states that when the president comes to parliament, he does only two things. You have to tell the country steps taken and progress achieved in the realization of the values under Article 10,”Sifuna noted.
The Nairobi Senator, who said he has consistently stayed away from the annual presidential address since his election, described the occasion as a platform Ruto uses to make claims about government achievements while overlooking concerns surrounding governance and accountability.
He took issue with what he termed the President’s tendency to highlight development projects, citing the construction of a market in Homa Bay as an example, while failing to adequately address human rights concerns.
Sifuna specifically invoked the death of Albert Ojwang, a teacher and blogger from Homa Bay who died in police custody in June 2025, arguing that development announcements should not overshadow questions about the protection of citizens’ rights.
“So ever since I was elected, I said that because Kasongo’s (President Ruto) work is to lie about those things of his, I don’t attend that State of the Nation address ,someone said it’s called the ‘State of Imagination’, right? Because he will go there to tell you, ‘Oh, we built a market over there in Homa Bay,’ while forgetting he killed Albert Ojwang from Homa Bay,”Sifuna expressed.
He further accused the President of overlooking the country’s human rights record, insisting that accountability for deaths in police custody, protection of civil liberties and respect for the rule of law should form the centrepiece of the national address.
“You know the values under Article 10: human rights, the rule of law, equality, freedom of citizens, and public participation values. We are talking about sustainable development; you don’t tell us about roads,”
“ You tell us what steps you have taken as a government to ensure there is respect for human rights, that there is the rule of law, and that there is democracy in this country, as well as what progress has been achieved,”the Nairobi senator insisted.
Under Article 132(1)(c) of the Constitution, the President is required to report annually on measures taken and progress achieved in realising the national values under Article 10, publish details of the report in the Kenya Gazette and submit a report to the National Assembly on the country’s international obligations.
Article 10 identifies national values including the rule of law, democracy, participation of the people, human dignity, equity, social justice, inclusiveness, equality, human rights and sustainable development.
Sifuna also used the occasion to outline what he said would be his priorities should he become President after the 2027 General Election.
He pledged that his administration would prioritise the protection of human rights, democratic freedoms and the rule of law, arguing that the President’s responsibility should go beyond announcing development projects.
“When we take the helm next year, when I go to Parliament as the President of this nation, my job will be to explain the steps our government has chosen or taken to ensure there is respect for human rights, there is democracy in our country, there is freedom for citizens and there is the rule of law,” he said.
His remarks came as Ruto delivered his fourth State of the Nation Address before a joint sitting of the National Assembly and Senate, less than nine months before the August 2027 General Election.
The President used the address to defend his administration’s economic record, citing improvements in the exchange rate, reduced inflation, lower commercial lending rates and increased foreign exchange reserves.
He also presented infrastructure expansion, education reforms and employment opportunities as evidence of progress under his Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda.
The address came amid growing political scrutiny of Ruto’s performance, with the cost of living, taxation, unemployment, corruption and delivery of development projects remaining major concerns ahead of the next election

Oscar Piastri will serve a grid penalty in Las Vegas; McLaren confirm upgraded floor to be added to MCL40 at late stage of season; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifyin
items.text:
Oscar Piastri to serve grid penalty at Las Vegas GP as McLaren confirm addition of more upgrades to MCL40
Oscar Piastri will serve a grid penalty in Las Vegas; McLaren confirm upgraded floor to be added to MCL40 at late stage of season; watch the Las Vegas GP weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
Wednesday 18 November 2026 15:12, UK
McLaren have confirmed that Oscar Piastri will serve a 10-place grid penalty at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix as he will be forced to exceed his engine allowance for the season.
Following an unspecified reliability issue, Piastri will need to use his fifth Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) of the season, taking him beyond the limit of four that each driver has for the season.
A team statement said: "Oscar will take a new Internal Combustion Engine in Las Vegas after a reliability issue.

"As it is his fifth of the season, he will take a 10-place grid penalty, but he has a good chance to recover positions with overtaking in Saturday's race."
The Las Vegas Strip Circuit features a 1.2-mile straight that drivers take flat out, which should present a good opportunity for Piastri to surge back through the field.
McLaren also confirmed that both Piastri and his team-mate Lando Norris will have their cars fitted with a new turbo specification, which has been made available by the power unit supplier Mercedes following an engine upgrade.
"Both cars, as with the other HPP-powered cars, will be fitted with a new ADUO-enabled turbo specification," the team added. "The expected performance benefit is relatively small."
McLaren to bring new floor to Las Vegas
Despite there being just three rounds remaining of the 2026 season, McLaren will continue to upgrade their car with a new floor arriving in time for Las Vegas.
Having officially been dethroned as constructors' champions by Mercedes last time out in Brazil, McLaren are attempting to close down a 17-point deficit to Red Bull in the battle for third in this year's standings.
A McLaren statement said: "The team will bring further developments to the MCL40 as they continue to push to unlock more performance in the remaining races, primarily a new floor.
"We will also have some solutions to improve drag during the Free Practice sessions, which we will then review before making a decision on whether to run them on Friday.
"With plenty of opportunities to exploit the car's potential, both through evaluating the new upgrades and refining how to operate the package at the maximum potential available, the priority is to turn those learnings into performance on track and valuable points in the immediate term."
McLaren were the only member of F1's 'big four' teams to bring upgrades to Brazil, where the new parts helped Norris win the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
Ross Hood, McLaren executive director of programme delivery, said: "Our programme delivery has evolved throughout this year and continues to do so.
"The new regulations, combined with the volume and pace of performance coming from the tunnel and engineering through to the circuit, have made it an intense year. That galvanises the team and brings us closer together, so we get the right performance to the track while challenging each other and our ideas.
"A new floor is arriving in Las Vegas this week, and it's a great example of our programme delivery. The collaboration between Aerodynamics, Design, Performance, Planning and Manufacturing helped ensure the team could maximise the output of the last tunnel runs for the 40A. It's a big push, but by making decisions closely together, we hit the targets we set ourselves."

items.text:
Rico Verhoeven: Could the kickboxing superstar step in to fight Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua bill?
Rico Verhoeven could potentially step in to fight Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11; Cruiserweight star Jai Opetaia was originally due to box Wilder in a heavyweight contest but had to withdraw
Wednesday 18 November 2026 15:10, UK
Deontay Wilder is now looking for a new opponent for his fight on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard.
Wilder was due to box Jai Opetaia at the Principality Stadium on December 11, but Opetaia had to withdraw from their heavyweight bout and will stay at cruiserweight.
Wilder will remain on the card but the race is on to select a new opponent for him.
Rico Verhoeven could be a viable candidate. A kickboxing superstar, earlier this year the Dutchman went straight into a world title fight with legendary Ukrainian Oleksandr Usyk.
Verhoeven performed surprisingly well in that WBC championship fight in Giza. Although he was stopped in the 11th round, he had looked to threaten a monumental upset.
The Dutchman is now considering his next move and his team didn't rule out stepping in for Opetaia to fight Wilder in December.
"Plenty of interesting things happening right now," Verhoeven's manager Karim Erja told Sky Sports.
"We're exploring some exciting options for Rico, but you know him, he's always up for a big fight.
"Let's see what happens in the coming few days."

items.title: Ruto promises public order reforms, accountability for police abuses
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto has pledged reforms in public order management, promising improved police training, operational oversight and accountability amid mounting scrutiny over deaths and injuries during protests and confrontations with security agencies.
Addressing Parliamen
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto has pledged reforms in public order management, promising improved police training, operational oversight and accountability amid mounting scrutiny over deaths and injuries during protests and confrontations with security agencies.
Addressing Parliament during his State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said the government was strengthening systems for managing public order through improved professional standards, officer welfare, appropriate equipment, clear operational command, de-escalation procedures and stronger oversight.
“We are now strengthening the systems through which public order is managed. This includes improved training, professional standards, officer welfare, appropriate equipment, clear operational command, de-escalation procedures and stronger oversight,” he told lawmakers at a joint sitting of the National Assembly and the Senate.
The President acknowledged the painful events of the June 2024 anti-Finance Bill protests and subsequent demonstrations, during which Kenyans lost their lives, others sustained serious injuries and families suffered lasting trauma.
He also cited the breach of Parliament, attacks on public institutions, including the Judiciary, and the looting of businesses, saying the events had demonstrated the importance of stability to the country’s economic progress.
“Our security agencies have a constitutional mandate to secure human life and property,” Ruto said, adding that the exercise of that mandate must respect constitutional requirements.
“But we must also be unequivocal about the responsibility of the State. Where security officers use unlawful force or exceed their authority, wrongdoing must be acknowledged and those responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law,” he said.
The scale of fatalities during demonstrations has remained a major concern.
The Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) has reported 127 deaths across three major protest periods: sixty-two during the 2024 anti-Finance Bill demonstrations, twenty-seven during the June 2025 protest commemorations and thirty-eight during the July 2025 Saba Saba (July 7) demonstrations.
Separately, Missing Voices rights alliance documented twenty-four police-related killings in May 2026, twenty-one of them linked to protest policing.
The organisation attributed niineteen deaths to demonstrations against fuel price increases on May 18 and 19 across several counties, including Nairobi, Kiambu and Nakuru.
Article 37
Ruto said the right to peaceful assembly and protest remained protected under the Constitution, specifically Article 37, which guarantees every person the right to assemble, demonstrate, picket and present petitions to public authorities peacefully and unarmed.
“Article 37 of our Constitution guarantees the right of every person, peaceably and unarmed, to assemble, demonstrate, picket and present petitions to public authorities. We must always protect that right. Kenyans must remain free to express disagreement and criticise their Government,” he said.
On compensation, the President said the government had allocated Sh2 billion towards redress for victims of protest-related violations, including incidents dating back to 2017.
He told Parliament that by July 2026, the Compensation Panel had reported payments totalling Sh1.2 billion to 1,476 verified beneficiaries, including families of those killed and survivors who sustained serious injuries.
The breakdown provided in his address listed 1,036 civilian victims and 356 police officers injured in the course of their duties, figures which add up to 1,392 rather than the stated 1,476 beneficiaries.
Ruto said compensation was an important acknowledgement of harm but could not replace criminal accountability.
“For both the demonstrators and police, no compensation can restore a lost life or erase the suffering of a family. But acknowledging harm and providing lawful redress are important responsibilities of a State that respects its citizens,” he said.
“Equally, compensation does not replace accountability. Investigations must continue, and prosecutions must follow for violations of the law, wherever the evidence warrants.”
The progress of investigations has itself faced scrutiny. IPOA has previously cited forensic capacity constraints, including bottlenecks at the National Forensic Laboratory and Government Chemist, as well as evidentiary challenges slowing investigations into police-related deaths.
By June 2026, the authority had reported three cases before courts and another three forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) also condemned a shoot-to-kill directive issued by the Coast Regional Police Commander Ali Nuno in February 2026, describing it as unconstitutional and calling for accountable policing.
In August, Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja warned police commanders that they would be held responsible for deaths in custody and misconduct by rogue officers, following concerns raised by rights groups.
The President said the government’s objective was to establish a professional security service capable of preventing violence and protecting lives and property while safeguarding constitutional freedoms.
“The lesson of our experience is clear. Security and liberty are not opposing national objectives. They are complementary constitutional responsibilities and obligations,” he said.

items.title: Ruto tells Parliament Nairobi-Mombasa Highway dualling plan at advanced stage
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto says plans to dual the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway have reached an advanced stage, with the government targeting the expansion of the approximately 460-kilometre corridor as part of a wider programme to improve transport infrastructure and lower the cost o
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 — President William Ruto says plans to dual the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway have reached an advanced stage, with the government targeting the expansion of the approximately 460-kilometre corridor as part of a wider programme to improve transport infrastructure and lower the cost of doing business.
In his State of the Nation Address to Parliament on Wednesday, Ruto said arrangements for the dualling of the highway were at an advanced stage, without providing a detailed implementation timetable or the proposed financing structure.
The announcement follows a November 12 pledge in Mombasa, where the President said the government had finalised a framework to undertake the expansion within 12 months, without introducing new taxes or increasing public debt.
The project is expected to widen the existing two-lane highway to at least four lanes, with controlled entry and exit points.
Reports on the proposed design also indicate that the expanded corridor could operate as a toll road, raising questions about the cost motorists may ultimately bear.
The National Treasury is reportedly evaluating bids for a transaction adviser to assess traffic demand, engineering requirements, environmental considerations and project costs.
The Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) has put the estimated cost at approximately Sh300 billion, with construction expected to take about five years from commencement.
The proposed upgrade marks a shift from the earlier plan for the Sh468 billion Usahihi Expressway, a new highway proposed by US firm Everstrong Capital.
National Treasury’s Public-Private Partnerships Committee rejected the proposal in July 2025, in a decision subsequently upheld by a tribunal in April 2026.
Upgrading the existing A8 corridor is expected to avoid some of the land acquisition requirements associated with constructing a new highway.
The Motorists Association of Kenya has called on the government to make the proposed deal public, particularly its financing structure and the implications for road users, amid the President’s assurance that the project will not impose an additional financial burden on citizens.
Some sections of the corridor are already undergoing or have completed dualling under KeNHA, including the Mombasa-Mariakani stretch and the Athi River-Machakos Turnoff section.
The Nairobi-Mombasa project forms part of Ruto’s broader infrastructure ambitions, including the target to tarmac 28,000 kilometres of roads and dual 2,500 kilometres of highways over the next decade.
The President said approximately 7,000 kilometres of roads were under construction, including projects that had stalled before his administration.
He argued that improved road infrastructure would reduce the cost of transporting agricultural produce and manufactured goods, connect workers to employment opportunities and improve access to schools and healthcare facilities.
Other priority corridors highlighted in the address include Rironi-Naivasha-Nakuru-Mau Summit, Kamandura-Maai Mahiu-Naivasha, Isiolo-Wajir-Mandera, Kenol-Marua, Lake Victoria Ring Road and Mau Summit-Eldoret-Malaba.
The government is also pursuing the extension of the Standard Gauge Railway from Naivasha through Narok and Bomet to Kisumu and Malaba, alongside modernisation of the ports of Mombasa and Lamu.

items.summary:
Israel row a 'defining moment for us' - Hallgrimsson
- Published
Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says the controversy surrounding the Nations League games against Israel has made "this group stronger".
The players took a vote on whether to play the two matches - in September and Octo
items.text:
Israel row a 'defining moment for us' - Hallgrimsson
- Published
Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says the controversy surrounding the Nations League games against Israel has made "this group stronger".
The players took a vote on whether to play the two matches - in September and October - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.
The Republic of Ireland won the first match 3-0 in Hungary before a 1-1 draw in Serbia.
Hallgrimsson was speaking after his side defeated 10-man Kosovo 3-0 in Dublin on Tuesday night to finish runners-up to Austria in Group B3.
The second place means the Republic of Ireland will be in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw next month and also ensures they have a promotion/relegation play-off in March against a League A team as they try to move up to the top tier for the first time.
"It tested everyone - physically, mentally and no I've learned a lot doubt and the players have learned a lot and grown," said Hallgrimsson.
"I am pretty sure in one year, two years when this team becomes successful we will look back and say that was the defining moment for us.
"I am pretty sure we will look back in hindsight and say this was a huge moment for us.
"Us as leaders sometimes artificially create us against the world to get the group to stick together and I have said we have got that environment for free for two or three weeks and we survived it and it made this team and this group stronger."
- Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo 
  - Published15 hours ago
- Talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals 
  - Published14 hours ago
Troy Parrott scored two penalties and Jack Moylan also netted against a Kosovo team hit by the dismissal of Kreshnik Hajrizi after 26 minutes.
It brought to an end a campaign which saw the Republic of Ireland win two matches, with two drawn and two lost.
"We know we will never be perfect and we are trying to find a way to win with what we have," Hallgrimsson added.
"I think we are getting better and better on that. Like I said in the first meeting when I was here and was introduced, I said I want to build a team that is difficult to play against and I feel like we are getting closer and closer to that.
"We are now consistent in our selection of players. We've more or less found our squad, our group and with doing that on a consistent basis, playing the same players together, playing the same system, the connections between players are starting to emerge."
The promotion/relegation play-off draw take place on Friday with the Republic set to go up against one of Croatia, Serbia, Denmark or Wales.
"Everybody, and especially us, like to play the top teams. For one, to compare yourself with the best teams, that's one thing," he said.
"Second, those teams will expose your weaknesses and that helps you in your growth to play these teams and they will expose your weaknesses so we can continue our growth. We're already looking forward to March.
"[There are] exciting teams in the pot. Whoever we draw, it's going to be two tough games and it's good for this team at this time to play these matches instead of friendlies, for example.
"So we're really excited for March and looking forward to meeting the players again."

items.title: South Africa Rugby condemns online abuse of officials after Erasmus ban
items.summary:
Nations Championship: South Africa Rugby condemns online abuse at officials following Rassie Erasmus six-match ban
South Africa condemn online abuse of World Rugby officials following Rassie Erasmus six-Test ban; Springboks head coach received suspension for comments following Nations Championship d
items.text:
Nations Championship: South Africa Rugby condemns online abuse at officials following Rassie Erasmus six-match ban
South Africa condemn online abuse of World Rugby officials following Rassie Erasmus six-Test ban; Springboks head coach received suspension for comments following Nations Championship defeat to France, claiming 'match-fixing' and more; SA Rugby has requested full misconduct hearing
Wednesday 18 November 2026 13:14, UK
South Africa Rugby has condemned online abuse of World Rugby officials following the decision to hand Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus a six-match ban.
An independent panel imposed the punishment after reviewing comments made by Erasmus at a media conference on Monday ahead of the Nations Championship match against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday.
SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing for the 54-year-old, who will not be able to have any matchday involvement in international fixtures during the suspension.
Erasmus delivered an outspoken press conference on Monday, in which he suggested officials had missed 17 illegal tackles against his side during their crunch Nations Championship clash. He went as far as questioning whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" of the result was behind why those incidents were not picked up.
World Rugby confirmed it had reviewed the comments made by Erasmus, and an independent panel had imposed the sanction under World Rugby's Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, a framework that was introduced in July.
Following a social media backlash against the global governing body, SA Rugby has called for calm to allow the proper processes to run their course.
"SA Rugby is aware of the extensive public commentary, analysis and debate surrounding recent matters involving Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus and World Rugby," a statement from the organisation read.
"We are mindful that a significant volume of commentary, opinion and AI-generated content is currently circulating in the public domain, much of which does not necessarily reflect the facts, context or processes involved.
"What is deeply concerning, however, is the reaction of some individuals on social media and other platforms, particularly reports of threats and abusive conduct directed at World Rugby officials and administrators.
"SA Rugby unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats or personal attacks. Such behaviour has no place in rugby and is entirely contrary to the values upon which our game is founded.
"Rugby has long been recognised as a sport built on respect, discipline, integrity and sportsmanship. These values extend beyond the field of play and apply equally to players, coaches, match officials, administrators and supporters. While robust debate and differing opinions are part of sport, they must always be expressed respectfully and responsibly.
"SA Rugby also wishes to assure all stakeholders that rugby possesses the necessary expertise, experience and governance structures to deal with matters of this nature appropriately.
"Any issues that arise will be addressed through the established rugby processes and by the individuals entrusted with these responsibilities, ensuring that due process is followed and that the best interests of the game remain paramount.
"We remain committed to protecting the integrity of rugby, upholding its values and ensuring that all participants in the game are treated with dignity and respect."

items.text:
Ivan Toney loses bid to avoid Euro 2028 court clash
- Published
A bid to move the date of England striker Ivan Toney's assault trial to avoid a clash with Euro 2028 has been refused.
The 30-year-old footballer, from Northampton, is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on 6 December.
Toney denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a trial of up to four days was fixed for 12 June 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.
He represented England at this summer's World Cup and has made 10 international appearances. It is not yet known if he will be selected for Euro 2028, but the application was made in case.
At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, where Toney did not appear, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: "It came to our attention that… there may be potentially a football match called the European Championship in 2028 between 9 June and 9 July."
Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: "We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.
"My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup."
Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a "speculative" application.
He refused the request, saying: "It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed."
The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.
Toney missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.
Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.
He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

items.summary:
Joint-record six referee errors in last Premier League weekend
- Published
The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled there were six on-field errors in the last round of games - the joint-highest it has recorded in one weekend.
Each week, the five members of the panel assess all the co
items.text:
Joint-record six referee errors in last Premier League weekend
- Published
The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled there were six on-field errors in the last round of games - the joint-highest it has recorded in one weekend.
Each week, the five members of the panel assess all the contentious incidents and vote whether both the referee and the video assistant referee (VAR) have got the decisions correct.
You have to go back to the early part of the 2023-24 season to find the last time there were six mistakes logged.
The statistic does not include correct VAR interventions to fix errors, such as the red card shown to Brentford's Igor Thiago.
In the last round of games almost every fixture had a contentious refereeing situation which was hotly debated.
It started on Friday with a potential penalty to Coventry City for a hair pull by Everton's James Tarkowski.
Arsenal were denied a penalty following a VAR review after it was deemed Kai Havertz was offside.
Tottenham lodged a complaint over a challenge by Leeds United's Jayden Bogle, who was not shown a red card.
And Liverpool argued against a late Crystal Palace penalty.
But which decisions did the KMI Panel rule were incorrect? Some of the votes might surprise you.
Two decisions were on-field and VAR errors
Such was the controversy across the weekend, it may come as a surprise that the KMI Panel ruled only two were missed VAR interventions. There have been six missed overall, the same number as this stage last season.
Incident 1: Coventry's Caleb Yirenkyi appeared to have his hair pulled inside the area by Everton's James Tarkowski. No penalty was awarded.
KMI Panel vote: 5:0 incorrect, for the on-field decision and the VAR.
What the KMI Panel said: "Tarkowski had a hold of Yirenkyi's hair and the panel unanimously felt that VAR should have intervened."
Incident 2: Arsenal's Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Hull City's Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international.
KMI Panel vote: 5:0 incorrect, for the on-field decision and the VAR.
What the KMI Panel said: "Although Harvertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence."
Four decisions were on-field errors, but not VAR mistakes
When the KMI Panel sits down to vote there are two separate considerations.
The first is on the decision of the referee, which is a basic judgement in law and the Premier League's expected interpretation.
The second is on the potential VAR intervention. This takes into account what the referee has said, the available replay angles and the high bar for intervention.
Incident 1: Thierno Barry put Everton in front against Coventry in the 61st minute, but there was a VAR check for a potential handball.
KMI Panel vote: 2:3 incorrect on the field, but 5:0 no VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "On the balance of probability the ball did accidentally strike Barry's hand. However, the readily available footage did not provide conclusive evidence."
Incident 2: Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty against Liverpool three minutes into stoppage time for a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio. But was it just a clash of heads?
KMI Panel vote: 0:5 incorrect on the field, but 5:0 no VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "A penalty was incorrect with the contact being inevitable. However, it was not a clear and obvious error."
Incident 3: Ipswich were awarded a 72nd-minute penalty against Bournemouth for a foul by Lewis Cook on Abdoul Ouattara.
KMI Panel vote: 1:4 incorrect on the field, but 4:1 no VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "Ouattara made a clear step across Cook who didn't make a challenge and the referee's decision to award a penalty was incorrect. However, it was not a clear and obvious error."
Incident 4: Potential second yellow card for Bournemouth's Marcus Tavernier.
KMI Panel vote: 2:3 incorrect on the field; no VAR intervention possible.
What the KMI Panel said: "There was a clear, deliberate action by Tavernier to delay the restart."
The controversial decisions deemed to be correct
Some of the most high-profile decisions from across the weekend have not yet featured.
That is because they have been voted to be correct on the field and through VAR.
Incident 1: Leeds United's Jayden Bogle caught Tottenham's Mathys Tel on high on his ankle. There was no VAR review for a red card.
KMI Panel vote: 3:2 correct on the field and for the VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "The majority felt Bogle was looking to challenge with his right leg and his left leg came down on the back of Tel's ankle without the speed, force or intensity to be serious foul play. Two panellists felt that the challenge was sufficiently dangerous to merit a red card."
Incident 2: Chelsea's Cole Palmer went down on the edge of the area under a challenge by Sunderland's Luke O'Nien.
KMI Panel vote: 4:1 correct on the field and for the VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "Clear contact made by O'Nien on Palmer which the panel felt should have been penalised with a free-kick on the basis that contact was made outside the area. One panellist felt that the foul contact was inside the area."
Incident 3: Sunderland were awarded a penalty when Levi Colwill was ruled to have tripped Brian Bobbey.
KMI Panel vote: 5:0 correct on the field and for the VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "There was upper body holding from both players as they progressed into the penalty area before a careless trip by the Chelsea defender."
Incident 4: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser.
KMI Panel vote: 5:0 correct on the field and for the VAR intervention.
What the KMI Panel said: "Although Lammens turned away from the ball, the contact he made on Suzuki was not impactful."

items.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
items.summary:
The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.
Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardi
items.text:
The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.
Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.
There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.
Multiple sources have confirmed that Netflix will submit a bid ahead of Thursday’s deadline for first-round offers, along with fellow streamers Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and Dazn, as well as the traditional broadcasting heavyweights, Fox, ESPN, NBC Universal and Paramount Skydance, although the latter may find itself constrained by the ongoing budget cuts being made after its $110bn acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Netflix has already bought exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cup.
“There’s a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes,” one broadcasting veteran says. “All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights.”
In a significant change, Fifa is selling the English and Spanish rights together for the first time in an attempt that indicates it is seeking a single exclusive rights holder, which would suit the streaming companies. With Fox having paid $485m for exclusive English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup, and NBC Universal’s Telemundo paying $600m for the Spanish-language rights, the only certainty is that the 2030 price will be far higher, despite less attractive kick-off times for a US audience with the tournament in Morocco, Spain and Portugal.
The impact of the time difference is hard to price, but may not prove to be that significant given the seemingly insatiable demand. NBC paid about $1.5bn for exclusive rights for the 2024 Paris Olympics and were rewarded with average daily viewing figures of more than 30 million, albeit with far more variation in programming than a World Cup.
Fifa awarded non-competitive extensions to Fox and Telemundo in 2015 as compensation for moving the 2022 Qatar World Cup to winter, a perspective that was strengthened on the back of this year’s record-breaking tournament. Fox’s live coverage of Spain’s extra-time victory over Argentina in the final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history, with a peak audience of 51.685 million; five World Cup games brought in average audiences of more than 20 million; and the average viewing figure across all 104 matches was 7.7 million, twice the figure in Qatar four years earlier.
Telemundo’s coverage, available through NBC’s streaming platform Peacock, averaged a total audience of six million viewers per game, with both Spain v Argentina and Mexico v England attracting peak audiences of more than 23 million, the highest-ever for a Spanish-language broadcast in the US.
The bumper audiences were extremely lucrative for the broadcasters, with figures from advertising sales analysts Guideline showing that Fox and Telemundo generated a combined $1.19bn in advertising revenue alone during the tournament, almost three times the figure from Qatar four years earlier and more than their original rights investment.
Fox alone brought in $835m from World Cup advertising, with 30-second slots costing between $200,000 and $750,000 according to the Hollywood Reporter, and the six-minute hydration breaks generating between $2m and $9m per game.
Having left a considerable amount of money on the table due to the circumstances of the 2026 process, Fifa is determined to cash in this time around. Holding the auction only four months after the US hosted the World Cup appears a clear attempt to capitalise on the success of the previous tournament, which contributed the vast majority of Fifa’s $4bn media revenues over the four-year cycle to 2026.
The addition of hydration breaks will give the likes of Fox more revenue to play with, although Fifa will expect the option for extra adverts to drive up the price and take its own cut this time around having missed out in the summer. The two three-minute breaks in each half were only finalised last year and did not feature in the 2026 tender documents.
“Sports advertising is much more valuable than entertainment programming as it has a broader reach,” saysFrançois Godard, an independent media analyst. “And one-off events such as World Cups do not generally do particularly well for subscription services, who want year-round content.
“Fox in particular needs the World Cup and is heavily associated with it. They are the smallest of the legacy broadcasters and are reliant on sport, as well as news. Having said that, the market for sport amongst streamers is far more competitive in the US than in Europe. Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have all bought NFL rights, while Apple is investing heavily in Formula One, so I wouldn’t rule any of them out.”
Adam Kelly, president of global sports marketing agency IMG, has a seat at the table at many rights negotiations and has long predicted the rise of the streamers, viewing the 2030 World Cup as the potential tipping point when a premium event could be exclusively bought in a major market by a streaming service for the first time. IMG has the rights to sell more than 70 global sports organisations, including the Premier League, World Rugby and Wimbledon.

items.title: ‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi
items.summary: “I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few
items.text:
“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.
Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.
“I’d get asked to go to a job or I’d even get booked for a job and they’d be like: ‘Oh, we want you to come to Germany for three days,’” Sowunmi says. “But I had to say: ‘I can’t do it, my priority is football.’ As fun and different as [modelling] is, it’s not my main job. Football was my priority and is my priority.
“It’s wicked, the stuff I’ve done modelling. Going to Milan fashion week, being taken to Paris fashion week with brands like Christian Louboutin is a level that I never thought I would reach or be possible when I first started it. Some of the people I’ve met doing it … when I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West … just celebrities and people that I grew up listening to and I feel like without that it probably wouldn’t have happened.”
Sowunmi takes a pilates class twice a month in the five-star Nobu hotel in central London. He is an imposing presence at 1.98m (6ft 6in) tall and grimaces through the session as his muscles are put to the test to keep him in shape for both his professions. It helps him to battle robust strikers and appear on social media as part of modelling campaigns. “Two days ago one of my current coaches said: ‘You popped up wearing a coat on my Instagram the other day. Can you get me one?’” Sowunmi says. “But I had to explain that it doesn’t really work like that.”
Sowunmi’s career path since he left his first club, Ipswich, without making an appearance has been that of a true lower-league player, taking in spells at Yeovil, Colchester and – between two stints with Bromley – Sutton. On the catwalk, he has rubbed shoulders with some of the biggest names in the industry while promoting designer brands and plans to continue doing that once he retires from the day job. He uses social media not only to post videos and images from photoshoots but to show the reality of life as a footballer.
“The fans and everyone that watches you on Saturday or Tuesday or whatever day you’re playing, they get to see you for 90 minutes and they don’t see the full dedication that goes into being a professional footballer,” Sowunmi says. “We’re away from our families for two days [for away games]; we’ll train on the Friday then leave, maybe have a seven-hour coach journey. We’ll have stuff to do at the hotel, stretching sessions, pool sessions, nutrition. We’ll wake up and we’ll have more stuff to do and it’s that whole buildup that I kind of want to show them and give them an insight into what we do.”
Last season Sowunmi helped Bromley gain promotion to third tier for the first time. The step up has been difficult, costing the long-serving manager Andy Woodman his job. “It’s been tough, as you can tell by the league position,” Sowunmi says. “It’s a completely different league. It’s taken a lot of the players by surprise, the difference between League One and League Two, but we’re grinding, we’re working hard and I’m sure it will turn for us.”
A carefully curated moustache sits atop Sowunmi’s lip to raise money for Movember. He is speaking at a charity event on Wednesday to highlight the importance of mental health, a subject close to his heart since his best friend took his own life. “It’s something that is really deep in my heart just being a voice for people and trying to help make a difference in any way that I can,” Sowunmi says. “I was actually on an away trip and I received a call from his dad to give me the news.
“Everyone was asking me what was wrong on the bus and that I wasn’t really speaking to anyone and then I think when we got home it was a four-, five-hour journey. The manager took me to the side and got me to open up to him a little bit. Looking back that actually helped a lot, so I thought if I can help someone to speak to someone or know that it’s fine to speak to someone then I’m definitely here for it.”

items.title: Man Utd expected to back Poch in January transfer window
items.summary:
Man Utd transfer news: Calvin Bassey and Jarrad Branthwaite among targets with Mauricio Pochettino set to be backed in January

items.text:
Man Utd transfer news: Calvin Bassey and Jarrad Branthwaite among targets with Mauricio Pochettino set to be backed in January
Watch our 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special on Sky Sports News at 4pm and 7pm as we look ahead to January; Man Utd are expected to be active in the market with left-back, centre-back and a forward on the agenda for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino
Tuesday 17 November 2026 20:11, UK
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.
A left-back, centre-back and forward are areas the club are looking to potentially strengthen in January with Pochettino expected to have input on targets they will pursue.
Despite the club's hierarchy feeling the team should be further up the table, there is also an acknowledgement that they could have further strengthened the squad in the summer in areas where they lacked depth.
Sky Sports News understands Manchester United already had plans to move in the upcoming window under former head coach Michael Carrick, before he was sacked last month following United's worst start to a league season for 40 years.
However, Pochettino is now expected to be consulted in the coming weeks and will have his say on potential recruits in January.

Centre-back
Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite are two players United are monitoring as potential options to reinforce their defence in January.
Despite Fulham's struggles this season, Bassey is a player who has impressed and has just six months left on his current deal, though his club have the option to extend that by a further year.
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has described the 26-year-old as one of the best defenders in the world and said the club's aim is to extend Bassey's contract.
Meanwhile, Branthwaite has long been admired by United. In 2024, United had two bids rejected for the centre-back, their second being worth around £50m.
Everton are in a strong negotiating position over the 24-year-old, who has a contract until the summer of 2030.
United are looking at left-footed centre-back options as they consider potential replacements for Lisandro Martinez. His future at Old Trafford looks in doubt come next summer with his current contract expiring.
Despite United having an option for a further 12 months, he is unlikely to be offered fresh terms as Sky Sports News reported last month.
Left-back
The club decided not to pursue a left-back in the summer as they focused on their midfield rebuild with the belief their long-term targets would be more attainable next year.
It remains to be seen whether that will be true come the end of the season and where that leaves players such as Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, but with five different players being used in that position with limited success, the club will look at the possibility of cover at left-back in January.
Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson continues to be monitored, as first reported by Sky Sports News in March. Fulham are aware of widespread interest in Robinson but no club has so far made a move for the 29-year-old, who worked under Pochettino with the USA.
Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was a player linked with United in the summer but was never at a stage when the move seemed likely. United were aware of his potential availability and it has not been ruled out that they revisit a deal in January if it works for all parties.
Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri was an option United tentatively explore on Deadline Day but they decided against pursuing him due to City's insistence on an obligation to make the move permanent. Sky Sports News understands he is not considered a target at this stage as United look at other options.
Forward
With United's main No 9 Benjamin Sesko ruled out until at least January, the club will explore potential reinforcements in the upcoming window to re-balance the club's attack.
Although United scored seven goals in their last two games before the break, the club have missed a physical presence in Sesko's absence to lead the line.
Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a player of interest but his future looks likely to remain at Elland Road and United are not expected to explore a move for the forward.
Outgoings
Any outgoings in January could have an impact on how much the club can reinforce Pochettino's squad but numerous first-team departures are not likely with the size of the squad and long-term injuries as well as Pochettino needing time to assess his squad all set to play a factor.
Joshua Zirkzee continues to be a player who attracts interest from Italy and United could entertain a move for the Dutch forward if they receive a suitable offer but would need cover in that position.
Martinez's future will under the spotlight in January. Sky Sports News reported last month United are unlikely to offer him a new contract. His current deal expires next summer although the club hold an option for a further 12 months.
Pochettino will also have to manage other expiring contracts in his squad with Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and captain Bruno Fernandes also in the last six months of their current contracts, although it is worth noting the club have a 12-month option on Fernandes and Maguire.

Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez were pursued over the summer, but Arsenal failed to agree deals for any of their top forward targets.
Arsenal are believed to be moving on from Atletico Madrid's Alvarez as he is not keen to leave Spain. Meanwhile, Rogers signed for Chelsea in a £117m deal, a fee Arsenal were unwilling to reach, and Vinicius signed a new deal with Real Madrid.
Bournemouth's Alex Scott is also of interest to Arsenal, who are understood to be willing to move on a midfielder to beat Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature.
Aston Villa
Aston Villa ended the summer happy with their business after a window that, for a long time, looked like it would be a difficult one.
There were a host of high-profile departures but a string of arrivals to replace them have left Unai Emery with an exciting, younger squad and all positions filled.
One bit of unfinished business that will be arguably more important than the signing of any player is the new contract for manager Emery.
Bournemouth

Scott's departure is by no means a foregone conclusion in January but if he was to leave then Bournemouth would like to sign a midfielder.
Bournemouth want to ensure Marco Rose's squad is in a strong position to fight on in the Premier League and Europa League for the rest of the season before what is expected to be a big summer of upheaval.
Brentford
Brentford are continuing to monitor Archie Gray's situation at Tottenham. The club were interested in signing him in the summer and are keeping an eye on his rate of minutes under Roberto De Zerbi.
Gray has been a focal point of De Zerbi's team so far this season, making eight starts in their 10 games. He has found an opening at right-back due to Pedro Porro's injury.
Porro returned to the starting line-up against Leeds, which saw Gray start in midfield, as Spurs were beaten at Elland Road. Brentford will be keeping an eye on whether Gray keeps his place or finds minutes harder to come-by in the run up to the January window.
Brentford are not expected to be busy in January having improved their squad in the summer and made an excellent start to the campaign under Keith Andrews
Brighton
Brighton don't really have any "unfinished business" in terms of incomings from the summer to complete in January. They looked at a number of players in different positions and ended up signing a player in each role.
With Brighton's outstanding displays taking them to second in the table after 10 games, very little if anything is likely to happen in terms of first-team ready signings. Historically, owner/chair Tony Bloom prefers to do business in the summer when targets are more obtainable and more affordable than mid-season.
The January window is sometimes used to sign prospects from abroad and begin their development on the south coast. In terms of outgoings, they will not listen or entertain any offers for main first team squad players with the club being tipped as contenders for a Champions League place.
Some of the young players at the club may go out on loan for game time.
Chelsea
Manager Xabi Alonso remains open to signing another midfielder after the departure of Enzo Fernandez in the summer and seeing a Deadline Day deal for Monaco's Lamine Camara collapse.
Chelsea are interested in Bournemouth's Alex Scott and are believed to have the financial edge over other clubs in the race to sign the England international.
However, he is not Chelsea's only target while Romeo Lavia's improvement could reduce their urgency to reinforce their midfield options.
Coventry
Coventry City made 12 major signings and spent over £130m during the summer, but results so far suggest further investment will be needed at both ends of the pitch to boost their chances of retaining Premier League status.
One situation to watch could be the future of attacking midfielder Jack Rudoni - a player Coventry will be determined to keep hold of but who is attracting attention after an impressive start to the season.
Crystal Palace
Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez saw his proposed summer move to Crystal Palace break down after he had a medical. The Ecuadorian is yet to play this season, so any renewed January move by the south London club is thought to be unlikely.
Palace signed centre-backs Axel Disasi from Chelsea and Honest Ahanor from Atalanta on loan, plus free agent defender Takehiro Tomiyasu, but further additions in that area, and also up front, cannot be ruled out.
